decisions.reason: F2 cited exclusions (5)(i) without its global positive-definiteness premise; step 1.1 used that conditional result to establish positivity in 2.1. The repair derives the recurrence locally by two Laplace expansions, proves cos(pi/3)=1/2 from published trigonometric suppliers, and inducts to d_k=(k+1)/2^k before the final label-4 computation. The n=2 case uses d_0=1 and gives det(2C)=2; all leading minors are positive. Diagram equality and the intrinsic parabolic/type-A supplier apply with the stated ranks.

F1 omitted the exclusions lemma's global positive-definiteness premise, so the original recurrence citation did not justify either proving positivity of H3/H4 or testing the nonpositive neighbours. New step 1.2 proves the recurrence for arbitrary path matrices by two Laplace expansions with d_0=1. The trig polynomial factors as (t+1)(4t^2-2t-1)^2, positivity selects cos(pi/5)=(1+sqrt(5))/4, and the computed doubled H3/H4 determinants are 3-sqrt(5) and (7-3sqrt(5))/2. The excluded C determinants are (3-2sqrt(5))/16 and (3-3sqrt(5))/32; the star witness gives (1-sqrt(5))/8. All signs and Sylvester/finiteness applications satisfy their actual hypotheses.

Step 3.1 treated d_k both as leading minors of the labelled path and as all-3 determinants. For labels (4,3), i=1 and j=2, the original formula gives 0 using d_2=1/2, whereas direct Laplace expansion gives det C=1/4. The repair defines delta_k=(k+1)/2^k exclusively for all-3 subpaths and uses these throughout the j=1,2 and j>=3 induction. The resulting numerator is (i+1)(j+1)-4ij cos^2(pi/m), with denominator 2^(i+j). Also removed F3's unqualified citation to the positive-definite exclusions lemma; step 1.1 proves the recurrence independently, including d_0=d_1=1 and infinite-label coefficient 1. The arm identity B(w,u)=(p+1)u_p/2 holds even for p=1; completing squares gives residual 1-mu, positive exactly when the reciprocal sum exceeds 1. Finite arithmetic gives the listed strict and equality triples.
